supported_claims: The collection separates Mohanabansi, Bira Gitika and Sishu Kabita sections; it documents both political and children's writing.

Author memoir PDF66–67 calls Banambar his younger brother and explains using that name to avoid exposure to immediate arrest. Printed8/PDF67 identifies Mukura Press. Original draft nephew/Banamali reading was corrected after separate direct review.
Opening Mohanabansi poem printed9/PDF68 addresses Utkal as mother and invokes named writers/public figures; source supports restrained analysis of a public appeal.
limits: Do not turn the retrospective memoir into independently established police/archive facts.
Main text printed1 begins around PDF60; cite verified individual pages, not an assumed uniform offset throughout the volume.
Portrait and other images lack reuse permission; copyright is assigned to the memorial organization.
PDF4 gives 23 November 1896–28 April 1973; omit unnecessary dates rather than echo conflicting web biographies.
source_families.recommended_allocation: Up to 120 words for memoir and associated interpretation, leaving room for bibliographic note; do not add children's-poem discussion unless the actual pages are read.
source_families.quotation_limit: No extended poem quotation. At most 10 words if treated as song lyrics, otherwise 25 words verbatim per source; prefer original paraphrase.

source_families.title: Mo Desa, bound digitized issues
source_families.author_editor: Multiple contributors; original cover PDF31 explicitly credits editor Birakishore Das
source_families.publisher: Original imprint PDF30 identifies Ramaprasad Mohanty and Laxminarayana Press, Cuttack; hosted/digitized by Srujanika/Odia Bibhaba
source_families.publication_date: Exact Gregorian issue date not adopted; PDF31 indicates second year/fourth issue, while PDF3 belongs to a different first-year/third issue.

precise_locators: PDF31 original cover, lower-right editor credit
PDF32 contents credits Mo Gaon to Birakishore Das
PDF33–34 Mo Gaon poem with author signature at end
PDF5 story credited to Jaya Krushna Misra
PDF26 Khiri-Pitha credited to Upendra Tripathi
PDF27–28 Katha au Kama credited to Ramakrushna Nanda
supported_claims: Birakishore Das edited Mo Desa: visible original cover credit, not only modern catalogue metadata.

His signed Mo Gaon appears in the same bound archive, opening the issue represented by PDF31–34. Its speaker remembers a home village through soil, fields, water, birds and childhood, making a concrete companion to public patriotic verse.
The magazine includes other named writers and illustrated prose as well as poetry; editorial leadership does not make every contribution his.
limits: Do not call PDF1 a contemporary original editorial: it is a modern archive introduction.
Modern metadata description says 1946 but started_year says 1950; other sources say 1947. No launch-year claim adopted.
The bound scan joins issues; do not assign all inspected pages to the cover on PDF31.
No original print/illustration licence established. Do not reproduce magazine artwork as article media.
Do not label Mo Gaon a poem from Mo Chhabibahi or Nua Chhabibahi: no corresponding reader edition inspected.
source_families.recommended_allocation: About 140–170 words including note and restrained close reading; leave room for title/dek/brief reuse.
source_families.quotation_limit: Prefer paraphrase; no full stanza. Treat musical/lyric uncertainty conservatively with at most 10 quoted words.

source_families.title: Kavi Birakishore
source_families.source_type: Academy-published retrospective biography, drawing partly on earlier memorial literature and recollections; not an original schoolbook title page or government appointment record.
precise_locators: PDF6 author preface and consulted recollection sources
PDF38–40 printed31–33, journalism and editorship section
PDF40 printed33, paragraph immediately before the new heading about human values
supported_claims: Patnaik describes Birakishore's editing of Mo Desa as part of children's literary provision.

On printed33, Patnaik says the Odisha government entrusted him with textbook nationalisation and arrangements for textbook production/publication; children's literature was also an aim of that institution.
limits: Attribute the schoolbook-production account to Patnaik; do not inflate it into sole authorship of readers, a specific first edition or an official job title.
No original Mo Chhabibahi or Nua Chhabibahi title page located in bounded catalogue search. They remain unverified, not disproved.
Do not confuse publisher, editor, institutional production responsibility and author.
Earlier speculative page lead55–70 proved to concern poetry, not the schoolbook role; actual relevant locator is printed33/PDF40.
source_families.recommended_allocation: About 80–120 words including explicit attribution and note; enough for a clear publishing-role paragraph without unsupported book lists.
source_families.quotation_limit: At most 25 quoted words; no quotation needed.
